sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval continues to expose client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). No values are inferred from placeholders. MacroMicro direct retrieval was unavailable in this run. Current gaps are filled with official BLS/ISM/EIA evidence and current Reuters/authoritative reporting. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified. Fundamental holding scores do not move mechanically with macro/theme strength.
regime: Direct attacks on oil transportation around Iran/Hormuz have become the freshest macro shock, adding a stronger crude/product/shipping risk premium to an already inflationary regime. Resilient US jobs/services and restrictive yields remain the second major axis. Physical AI/power capex stays expansionary, while Iraq's export-capacity recovery is an important supply/rerouting offset.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Resilient jobs + strong services + expansionary manufacturing
channels.interpretation: August payrolls +162k with upward revisions, ISM Services 55.4 and Manufacturing 54.6 still support resilient demand. Weekend geopolitics does not change this underlying growth signal.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.interpretation: Strong labour/services and renewed energy inflation leave limited room for clean policy relief. Preserve Sep 4 market pricing until markets reopen; do not infer a weekend Fed-probability tick.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.regime: Long and short yields remain restrictive
channels.interpretation: Last valid cash-market evidence is 2Y ~4.37% and 10Y up to ~4.81% after payrolls. Financing remains expensive for housing, leveraged projects and long-duration equities.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.regime: Open for quality; costly for marginal borrowers
channels.interpretation: Quality issuers retain access, but high risk-free rates and AI/utility capital competition keep project hurdle rates elevated.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: The last verified CCC-and-lower yield reference around 14.6% remains punitive but dated. Exact live credit stress is not inferred.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.regime: Employment resilient; fuel and financing squeeze worsening
channels.interpretation: Payrolls support incomes, but record Labor Day gasoline and near-record diesel add a fresh purchasing-power squeeze. Consumer is resilient but increasingly energy-taxed.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: Last valid long-rate evidence remains hostile to mortgage affordability; no weekend data changes that conclusion.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.regime: Hard demand + geographic broadening + long-lead planning
channels.interpretation: Official ISM evidence validates transmission/generation spending, and the newly announced 1GW TCS/HyperVault campus independently confirms that AI infrastructure capex is broadening geographically. Prefer booked orders and FCF conversion over headline requested MW.

channels.label: AI Memory / Bandwidth
channels.regime: Near-term constrained supply; supply-response clock active
channels.interpretation: Memory/electronic components remain constrained in ISM evidence. No fresh weekend supply shock changes the existing thesis.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Energy, services and industrial cost pressure extreme
channels.interpretation: Services Prices 72.6, Manufacturing Prices 71.1, high fuel and tight copper/electrical/electronic/memory inputs keep input pressure at the top of the range.

channels.label: Labour
channels.regime: Broad payroll evidence improved despite services hiring caution
channels.interpretation: NFP +162k, unemployment 4.1% and upward revisions outweigh contractionary ISM Services Employment for the broad signal. Hiring is resilient rather than hot.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.regime: Mild risk-off at last cash close; weekend event risk elevated
channels.interpretation: Sep 4 equity declines were modest. Direct tanker strikes create Monday gap risk, but no weekend equity move is manufactured before markets reopen.

channels.label: Crude
channels.regime: Direct tanker attacks + Hormuz security premium
channels.interpretation: Direct U.S. strikes on three Iranian oil tankers and Iranian retaliatory shipping threats are a material escalation. Reuters reported Brent around $96.28. Iraq's >3 mbpd export capacity is the main offset and reinforces the need to model scarcity versus rerouting, not extrapolate a one-way spike.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.regime: Record consumer fuel stress remains dominant inflation channel
channels.interpretation: Labor Day gasoline is expected around a record $4.03/gal and diesel remains near record levels. Refined products remain more important for consumer/freight inflation than crude alone.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: Strategic LNG value; rerouting premium persists
channels.interpretation: No fresh U.S. gas scarcity signal was verified. Contracted LNG and pipeline infrastructure retain strategic value as buyers diversify away from vulnerable routes.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Geopolitical support versus high real-yield headwind
channels.interpretation: Weekend escalation improves the hedge case, but there is no new cash gold close. Real yields and USD remain the tactical gate, so the signal stays modest rather than being promoted mechanically.
